content: Bismuth subsalicylate is a medication prescribed to treat diarrhea, heartburn, and upset stomach in adults and children aged 12 years and older. It belongs to a class of medications known as antidiarrheal agents. The mechanism of action involves reducing the flow of fluids and electrolytes into the bowel, decreasing inflammation within the intestines, and potentially eliminating organisms that cause diarrhea. This medication is available in liquid, tablet, and chewable tablet forms, and it is taken orally, with or without food. It is essential to follow the instructions on the package carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take bismuth subsalicylate exactly as directed, without exceeding or reducing the recommended dosage or frequency. Swallow the tablets whole without chewing them. Shake the liquid form well before each use to ensure even mixing. If your symptoms worsen or if diarrhea persists for more than 48 hours, discontinue use and contact your doctor. Before taking bismuth subsalicylate, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to salicylate-based pain relievers such as aspirin, choline magnesium trisalicylate, choline salicylate (Arthropan), diflunisal (Dolobid), magnesium salicylate (Doan’s, others), or salsalate (Argesic, Disalcid, Salgesic), or any other medications. Additionally, disclose all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. This is particularly important if you are taking anticoagulants (blood thinners) like warfarin (Coumadin), daily aspirin, or medications for diabetes, arthritis, or gout. If you are taking tetracycline antibiotics such as demeclocycline (Declomycin), doxycycline (Doryx, Vibramycin), minocycline (Dynacin, Minocin), or tetracycline (Sumycin), ensure that these are taken at least one hour before or three hours after bismuth subsalicylate. Consult your doctor before using this medication if you have a history of ulcers, bleeding disorders, bloody or blackened stools, or kidney disease. Also, seek medical advice if you have a fever or mucus in your stool. If administering this medication to a child or teenager, inform their doctor if the child has symptoms such as vomiting, listlessness, drowsiness, confusion, aggression, seizures, yellowing of the skin or eyes, weakness, or flu-like symptoms. Additionally, notify the doctor if the child has not been drinking fluids normally, has experienced excessive vomiting or diarrhea, or appears dehydrated. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult their doctor before taking this medication. While taking bismuth subsalicylate, it is important to stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water or other fluids to replace those lost due to diarrhea. Unless otherwise instructed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet. If you forget a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. This medication is typically taken as needed. Bismuth subsalicylate may cause side effects, some of which can be serious. If you experience ringing or buzzing in your ears, stop taking the medication and contact your doctor immediately. If you notice any other unusual problems while taking this medication, consult your doctor. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. If you have any questions about bismuth subsalicylate, consult your pharmacist. You may notice darkening of the stool or tongue while taking this medication. This effect is harmless and typically resolves within a few days after discontinuing the medication.
